RECENT MONETARY AND FINANCIAL DEVELOPMENTS Haile Selassie Avenue P.O. Box 60000 - 00200 Nairobi \Tel: 20-2860000/2861000/ 2863000\Email: [email] CBKKenya Central Bank of Kenya www.centralbank.go.ke October 30, 2026 Inflation Inflation increased to 7.3 percent in October from 6.8 percent in September 2026, reflecting increases in both core and non-core components. Core inflation increased to 4.3 percent from 4.0 percent, driven by increased prices of select processed food items and transport costs. Non-core inflation increased to 15.1 percent from 14.0 percent, mainly due to a rise in prices of select fresh farm produce. Additionally, pump prices increased in the October pricing cycle reflecting higher international oil prices (Chart 1). Exchange Rates The Kenya Shilling remained stable against major international and regional currencies during the week ending October 29, 2026. It exchanged at KSh 129.96 per U.S. dollar on October 29, compared to KSh 129.91 on October 22 (Table 1). Foreign Exchange Reserves The foreign exchange reserves remained adequate at USD 14,740 million (5.9 months of import cover) as of October 29. This meets CBK’s statutory requirement to endeavour to maintain at least 4 months of import cover (Table 2). Money Market The money market remained liquid during the week ending October 29, and open market operations remained active. Commercial banks’ excess reserves averaged KSh 32.6 billion above the 3.25 percent Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) requirement. The Kenya Shilling Overnight Interbank Average (KESONIA) remained stable at 8.75 percent. During the week, the average number of interbank transactions decreased to 18 from 29 in the previous week, while the average value traded decreased to KSh 12.2 billion from KSh 19.8 billion in the previous week (Table 3). Government Securities Market The Treasury bill auction of October 29, received bids totalling KSh 51.9 billion against an advertised amount of KSh 28.0 billion, representing a performance of 185.2 percent. Interest rate on the 182-day Treasury bill declined while those on the 91-day and 364-day Treasury bills increased marginally (Table 4). Equity Market At the Nairobi Securities Exchange, the NASI increased by 4.16 percent while NSE 25 and NSE 20 declined by 2.97 percent and 2.61 percent respectively, during the week ending October 29. Market capitalization, total shares traded, and equity turnover decreased by 0.22 percent, 97.55 percent and 91.54 percent, respectively (Table 6). The significant decline in shares traded and equity turnover is due to the base effect of a block trade of KPLC shares in the previous week. Bond Market Bond turnover in the domestic secondary market increased by 3.57 percent during the week ending October 29, 2026 (Table 6). In the international market, yields on Kenya’s Eurobonds decreased by 22.07 basis points on average. Yields for Côte d’Ivoire and Angola also decreased (Chart 3). Global Trends As the inflation concerns remain, several central banks in advanced economies made their monetary policy decisions during the week ending October 29. While the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, US Fed, European Central Bank, Bank of Japan and Reserve Bank of New Zealand held their policy rates unchanged. The U.S. Dollar Index strengthened by 0.22 percent during the week. Murban crude oil prices rose to USD 110.46 per barrel on October 29, up from USD 108.23 per barrel on October 22, as geopolitical risks remain.
